explanation: At the current offset, try every nonempty prefix of the remaining text. Check that prefix by comparing mirrored characters (Python compares it with its reversal), recurse only on palindromes, and record a partition when all text has been consumed.
timeComplexity: O(n·2^n) worst-case time: there are at most 2^(n-1) partitions and substring testing/copying and materializing their pieces contribute a linear factor. At most 2^(n-1) cut subsets exist; recording a partition requires its pieces. The table variants additionally fill n² cells.
spaceComplexity: O(n) auxiliary live substring characters, recursion frames and partition entries; Java reuses the path list with add/remove. Returned partitions can occupy O(n·2^n).

correctness: The current pieces concatenate to exactly the consumed text and every piece is a palindrome. Every possible next cut is tested, so each legal partition follows exactly one branch. Reaching the end proves completeness of that partition; rejecting a nonpalindromic prefix loses no valid partition.
walkthrough: For pop, choosing single characters produces [p,o,p]. The entire substring pop is also palindromic, producing [pop]. No other next boundary yields a palindrome partition.
edgeCases: An empty string has one empty partition.
Repeated characters can create exponentially many valid partitions.
Character positions in this implementation are UTF-16 code units, not user-perceived grapheme clusters.
